name: RZText::CanStartLine
notes: A lazy static set (197 characters) in the original; here a sorted table. Called only from the cluster length (0x1b215d), in effect through it. RZTextBreak_CanStartLine compares every 16-bit value and 20000 random 32-bit values (the set's keys are 16-bit). Exercised through GZFont_Text as well. Mutation check (tools/mutate.py, lane OF, 2026-10-27): about 170 mutants over the line breaker, the widths, Layout, IsSpace, ThaiSign, HasThai, ToUtf16 and RZTextBreak.cpp (comparison and bound flips, dropped guards, swapped arguments and indices, changed constants); every one killed except these, argued equivalent or unreachable: in RZTextBreak.cpp six table or bound mutants that cannot change an answer (a boundary entry duplicated by its neighbour, a length bound never reached because the unit after the count is the terminator); in the line breaker the Thai cluster bound (count instead of count - consumed: the unit after the layout buffer is its NUL terminator, which is never a mark), the guard consumed < count before the layout-word comparison (a word at the end is the source length, which the last unit's word never equals), count != 0 in mode 1 (an empty conversion leaves the scan on the NUL terminator, which stops it at once), the previous-unit-is-not-a-space test of the space fix-up (a cluster swallows its trailing spaces, so a break never falls between two spaces), and a few redundant guards in the scan loops. Killed late by added ops (800 seeds): direct BreakLine and widths ops, GZFont_Predicates, GZFont_Layout, NUL right after the first unit, Thai texts starting with a consonant and sara am.
